evidence.section: 2 Experimental
evidence.quote: The NbMoTaWRe powders were prepared from pure Mo, Nb, Ta, W, Re element powders (purity approximately 99.5%) using a high-energy ball mill machine (QM-3SP4). In order to prevent powder oxidation, the whole process was carried out under high purity argon. The tungsten carbide vials and tungsten carbide balls were used as grinding media during ball milling. The ball-to-powder weight ratio was 20:1, and the milling speed was 400 r·min−1.

evidence.section: 2 Experimental
evidence.quote: The mechanically alloyed powders were prepared into bulk samples with a size of φ10 × 10 mm by using the SPS-211HT sintering system under a high purity argon atmosphere. The sintering conditions were sintering temperature of 1700–1900 °C, holding time of 20 min, and compaction pressure of 50 MPa, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.1 Characterization of the Mechanical Alloying Powders
evidence.quote: After ball-milling for 30 h, the diffraction peaks of the elemental metals were replaced by the diffraction peaks of a single BCC structure, indicating that the mechanical alloying was completed.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructural Analysis of the Sintered NbMoTaWRe Alloy
evidence.quote: The results show that with the sintering temperature increases from 1700 to 1900 °C, the grain size of the BCC matrix increases from 1.28 to 5.80 μm.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructural Analysis of the Sintered NbMoTaWRe Alloy
evidence.quote: It can be observed that the FCC precipitated phases are distributed at the grain boundaries of the BCC matrix, showing a semi-continuous network distribution... the average particle sizes of FCC precipitated phases are measured. The results show that as the sintering temperature increases from 1700 to 1900 °C, the average sizes of FCC phase increases from 0.66 to 2.98 μm. In addition, the volume fraction of the FCC phase and BCC phase can be obtained according to the phase maps. It shows that the volume fraction of the FCC phase increases slightly from 22.8 to 26.4%

evidence.section: 3.4 Mechanical Properties of the Sintered NbMoTaWRe Alloy
evidence.quote: The NbMoTaWRe RHEA bulk sintered at 1800 °C with an average grain size of 3.80 µm has the highest mechanical properties: σ0.2 = 2132 MPa, σp = 2630 MPa, εp = 6.82%.

evidence.section: 3.4 Mechanical Properties of the Sintered NbMoTaWRe Alloy

The average sizes of the (Nb, Ta)C particles in the bulk sintered at 1800 °C and 1900 °C are 1.97 μm and 2.98 μm, respectively.

evidence.quote: the presence of micropores is observed in the fracture morphologies, which induces local stress concentration and crack propagation resulting in the decrease of plasticity and ductility of the alloy.

evidence.section: 3.4 Mechanical Properties of the Sintered NbMoTaWRe Alloy
evidence.quote: the coarsening (Nb, Ta)C particles aggregate at the grain boundaries of the sample sintered at 1900 °C. In general, cracks tend to initiate and propagate around the large-size particles at the grain boundary during the deformation. Therefore, NbMoTaWRe alloy bulk sintered at 1900 °C with the aggregation of large size (Nb, Ta)C particles shows a lower elongation than that sintered at 1800 °C.
